activity.notes: Lê Lợi raised the Lam Sơn uprising in 1418 and led the anti-Ming war to victory in 1427. ATLAS uses Ming-occupied Đại Việt as an editorial historical political-community label for the Vietnamese side during Ming occupation; it does not imply that an independent sovereign Đại Việt state continuously existed throughout 1418-1427. The occupying Ming polity is not used as Lê Lợi's representative Polity.

sources.title: Tài trí của vua Lê Thái Tổ trong mười năm kháng chiến chống quân Minh (1418-1427) — Bảo tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia
sources.citation_text: Vietnam's National Museum of History states that Lê Lợi formally raised the Lam Sơn uprising in 1418, led the ten-year resistance against Ming forces, and secured their withdrawal at the end of 1427.

sources.title: Du xuân Lam Kinh – về miền địa linh tri ân bậc khai quốc — Bảo tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia
sources.citation_text: The National Museum describes Lê Lợi's Lam Sơn uprising as a 1418-1427 struggle that expelled Ming forces and opened a new era of independence for Đại Việt.
